proposals.before: At first Cang's father Chang was not full five chi tall; Cang was more than eight chi tall; Cang's son again was eight chi tall; reaching the grandson Lei was more than six chi tall.
proposals.after: At first Cang's father's height was not a full five chi; Cang was more than eight chi tall; Cang's son again was eight chi tall; reaching the grandson Lei, [he] was more than six chi tall.
proposals.reason: In 蒼父長不滿五尺, 長 means height/tallness, not a personal name; the literal invents a father named Chang.

proposals.before: Cang came; Marquis of Jiang and others honored and established Emperor Xiaowen; in the fourth year he replaced Guan Ying as chancellor.
proposals.after: Cang, with the Marquis of Jiang and others, honored and established Emperor Xiaowen; in the fourth year he replaced Guan Ying as chancellor.
proposals.reason: 蒼來絳侯等 is coordinate subjects (Cang and the Marquis of Jiang et al.), not “Cang came; Marquis of Jiang…”.

decisions.after: At first, Cang's father was not a full five chi tall; Cang was over eight chi tall; Cang's son was likewise eight chi tall; his grandson Lei was over six chi tall.
decisions.reason: Parallel 蒼長八尺餘, 蒼子復長八尺, and 孫類長六尺餘 shows that 長 means stature, not a father named Chang; the revised literal also removes the proposal's awkward bracketed pronoun.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 初蒼父長不滿五尺，蒼長八尺餘

decisions.after: Zhang Cang and the Marquis of Jiang and the others honored and installed the King of Dai as Emperor Xiaowen; in the fourth year, Cang replaced Guan Ying as chancellor.
decisions.reason: Wikisource and ctext preserve 蒼與絳侯等尊立代王為孝文皇帝: Cang jointly enthroned the King of Dai. The local 來 and omission of 代王為 are source defects, not wording to retain.

sourceWitness.citation: Hanshu 42, Zhang Cang biography; corroborated by ctext
sourceWitness.excerpt: 蒼與絳侯等尊立代王為孝文皇帝
